Where to eat and drink in Totterdown

Updated 2 November 2026. Places open, close and change hands, so check opening times before you go. We aren't paid to include anywhere. How we check facts.

Most of Totterdown's food and drink is on the Wells Road, the main road that climbs the hill from Three Lamps, with a handful of corner pubs on the side streets. Here's what locals and local guides recommend.

Quick answer

  • Pubs: the Oxford for a Sunday roast, the Shakespeare for cider, the Star & Dove or the New Found Out for sport, and the Thunderbolt for live music. [1]
  • Local beer: Bruhaha, a brewpub at 156–158 Wells Road brewing its own beers, including one named after Three Lamps. [2] [3]
  • Breakfast: a fry-up at Totterdown Canteen, 141 Wells Road. [1] [4]
  • Dinner: pizza at A Cappella or fish and chips at Farrows. [1]

What are the best pubs in Totterdown?

Totterdown pubs
PubKnown for
The OxfordA favourite with locals for its Sunday roast, plus live music and open mic nights [1] [5]
The Shakespeare, 1 Henry StreetCider, local art on the walls and a walled beer garden [1] [6] [7]
Star & Dove, St Luke's RoadFood and live sport; reopened under new management [1] [8] [9]
The New Found OutWatching live sport [1]
The Thunderbolt, 124 Bath RoadLive music in a Grade II listed former tollhouse [1] [10]

Is the Thunderbolt closing? The freehold has been put up for sale after 18 years under the same landlord, but Bristol24/7 reported it would keep trading and hosting live events until a sale completes. [11]

Where can you drink local beer in Totterdown?

  • Bruhaha, 156–158 Wells Road: started as a home brewery in 2019, ran pop-ups at Windmill Hill City Farm, and opened its permanent brewpub in October 2023 in the former Eat Your Greens café. [2]
  • Its beers include Three Lamps, an IPA, TotterDowner, a bitter, and Rusty Robot, a porter. [3]
  • Smokebox: smoked barbecue with cocktails. [12] [13]
  • BANK: coffee by day and cocktails and craft beer by night, in the former Banco Lounge on the Wells Road. [14] [15]
  • Carouse: a wine specialist. [15]

Where can you get breakfast in Totterdown?

  • Totterdown Canteen, 141 Wells Road: a traditional café for a cooked breakfast. [1] [4]
  • BANK: speciality coffee during the day. [14]

Where can you eat with children in Totterdown?

  • Tots & Teapots, Wells Road: a play café with sessions for young children, food and party bookings. [17]
  • Windmill Hill City Farm: a short walk away, with a café open every day and free entry to the farm. [18] [19] See parks and green spaces.

Where to eat during the Totterdown Arts Trail

Many local venues open specially or run pop-ups during the arts trail weekend, which is on 14 and 15 November in 2026. The organisers publish a food and drink list on their website, and the printed trail map is available in local businesses. [12] [15]
